name: Towards Computer-Using Personal Agents

name: OS-Kairos: Adaptive Interaction for MLLM-Powered GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses step-level confidence estimates to decide when a GUI agent should act autonomously or request human intervention in complex situations.

name: VeriSafe Agent: Safeguarding Mobile GUI Agent via Logic-based Action Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Translates user instructions into formal specifications and applies runtime logic-based checks to proposed mobile GUI actions.

summary: Evaluates security failures of computer-use agents under adversarial requests and screen-context manipulation. The study examines refusal behavior while agents perform tasks in desktop and web environments.

notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes a guardrail agent that reasons over explicit safety policies and checks action trajectories, with a web-agent safety benchmark.

name: A Survey of WebAgents: Towards Next-Generation AI Agents for Web Automation with Large Foundation Models
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Surveys foundation-model web agents through their architectures, training methods and trustworthiness. It organizes research on completing browser tasks from user instructions and identifies directions for further development.

name: Towards Trustworthy GUI Agents: A Survey
summary: Frames GUI-agent trustworthiness as an execution gap and reviews failures, attacks, and defenses across perception, reasoning, and interaction.

name: On the Robustness of GUI Grounding Models Against Image Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates GUI grounding models under natural image noise, untargeted adversarial perturbations, and targeted image attacks. Experiments cover mobile, desktop, and web interfaces and analyze sensitivity to image resolution and adversarial changes.

name: The Obvious Invisible Threat: LLM-Powered GUI Agents' Vulnerability to Fine-Print Injections
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Characterizes six forms of GUI-content injection and studies their effects on GUI agents and human users using adversarial webpages. The analysis examines privacy failures and the limits of human oversight.

name: DoomArena: A framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents a modular security testing framework that plugs into BrowserGym and tool-use benchmarks to evaluate agents under configurable threat models.

name: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a position paper proposing an evaluation framework.
summary: Presents a position paper on privacy and security evaluation for GUI agents, identifying risk categories and challenges in involving human evaluators. It proposes risk-aware assessment and in-context consent as design directions.

name: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WASP, an end-to-end benchmark for prompt-injection security in web agents. Its evaluation separates partial attack progress from completion of the attacker’s full objective.

name: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). The framework targets LLM agents broadly; web navigation is one attack outcome reported in the abstract.
summary: Introduces AgentVigil, a black-box fuzzing framework for finding indirect prompt injections against LLM agents, including attacks that redirect web navigation.

name: Characterizing Unintended Consequences in Human-GUI Agent Collaboration for Web Browsing
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies unintended consequences of collaborative web browsing with GUI agents through social-media analysis and interviews. It organizes observed failures, user impacts, and mitigation practices around planning, interface interaction, feedback, privacy, and trust.

name: A Survey on the Safety and Security Threats of Computer-Using Agents: JARVIS or Ultron?
summary: Systematizes safety and security threats to computer-using agents, with taxonomies of threats and defensive strategies.

name: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: Introduces WebInject, a prompt-injection attack that optimizes rendered webpage pixels to make screenshot-based web agents take attacker-chosen actions.

name: GEM: Gaussian Embedding Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Detection in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GEM detects instructions outside a GUI agent’s capabilities by modeling distances in its input-embedding space with a Gaussian mixture. Experiments across mobile, computer and browser data also examine selective escalation to a cloud model when an input is detected as unfamiliar.

name: From Assistants to Adversaries: Exploring the Security Risks of Mobile LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Analyzes security vulnerabilities across OEM system-level, third-party, and research mobile LLM agents, covering GUI and cross-application attack surfaces.

name: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Outlines an end-to-end threat model and empirical security evaluation across architectural layers of autonomous browser agents.

name: EVA: Evolving Semantic Adversaries for Red-Teaming GUI Agents Against Environmental Injection Attacks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces EVA, a red-teaming framework that evolves semantic payloads for GUI environmental-injection tests. It studies the contribution of semantic versus visual deception and distills discovered patterns into reusable evaluation rules.

name: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies backdoor risks in mobile GUI agents through AgentGhost, which combines goal-level and interaction-history triggers during model training. The paper evaluates multiple mobile agents and a tailored defense.

name: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies advertising delivery as an indirect-injection channel for web agents under a black-box threat model. AdInject evaluates how static ad content shaped by website context can redirect browser actions.

name: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RedTeamCUA combines a virtual-machine OS environment with containerized websites for controlled prompt-injection tests spanning both interfaces. Its RTC-Bench contains 864 examples and can initialize agents at injection points to separate attack susceptibility from navigation failures.

name: RiOSWorld: Benchmarking the Risk of Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces RiOSWorld, a computer-use risk benchmark separating user-originated and environmental threats. It evaluates both risky-goal intent and goal completion across web and other computer applications.

name: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained paper abstract; Android setup is supported separately by the official project README.
summary: Benchmarks truthfulness, controllability, safety, and privacy of multimodal LLM agents across interactive web and mobile GUI tasks.

name: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces VPI-Bench, interactive web-platform variants containing visually embedded malicious instructions. It evaluates computer-use and browser-use agents under these threats and examines system-prompt defenses.

name: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces VerificAgent, which grows domain-specific memories from task trajectories and subjects them to human fact-checking before deployment. Its OSWorld evaluation treats persistent memory as an auditable constraint on later agent behavior.

name: macOSWorld: A Multilingual Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Build the web for agents, not agents for the web

name: Poison Once, Control Anywhere: Clean-Text Visual Backdoors in VLM-based Mobile Agents

summary: Demonstrates clean-text visual backdoor attacks (VIBMA) that compromise fine-tuned VLM mobile agents through visual triggers while keeping text instructions intact.

notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Extends OSWorld with tasks covering user misuse, prompt injection, and model misbehavior, with assessment of both task success and safety.

name: Mobile GUI Agents under Real-world Threats: Are We There Yet?

notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a threat analysis with case studies.
summary: Analyzes security boundaries in computer-use agents through a risk taxonomy and concrete adversarial case studies. It links observed failures to input provenance, interface-action binding, memory, and delegation, and proposes CUA-specific evaluation principles.

name: OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates agent safety across real browser, code, filesystem, shell, and messaging tools using rule-based and model-based assessments.

name: VisualTrap: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack on GUI Agents via Visual Grounding Manipulation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies backdoors that redirect GUI visual grounding even when the task plan is correct. VisualTrap evaluates whether poisoned grounding training transfers to downstream tasks and across web, mobile, and desktop interface settings.

name: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces LaSM, a training-free defense that selectively scales attention and MLP components to improve alignment with task-relevant screen regions. It evaluates the approach against pop-up-based GUI injection attacks.

name: Machine-Readable Ads: Accessibility and Trust Patterns for AI Web Agents interacting with Online Advertisements

name: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebGuard, a human-annotated dataset for predicting outcomes and risk levels of state-changing website actions. It provides generalization splits and evaluates specialized guardrail models.

name: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree

summary: Studies indirect prompt injection through HTML content consumed as accessibility trees. The evaluation tests how manipulated page observations redirect browser-agent actions on real websites.

name: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems

name: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains

name: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents

summary: Introduces SAPA-Bench with 7,138 smartphone scenarios to evaluate whether MLLM-powered mobile agents detect and protect sensitive personal information on screen.

name: Throttling Web Agents Using Reasoning Gates
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The contribution is an access-cost mechanism spanning websites and MCP servers.

name: VeriOS: Query-Driven Proactive Human-Agent-GUI Interaction for Trustworthy OS Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies how GUI agents, people, and human-agent teams respond to manipulative interface designs. The two-phase evaluation examines failure modes and the benefits and costs of human oversight.

name: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Chameleon, an environmental-injection evaluation framework that varies webpage content and trigger context. It combines simulated page variation with attention-based optimization and tests GUI agents across realistic websites.

name: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces PrivWeb, which uses a local language model to anonymize interface information according to user preferences. Adaptive notifications and selective pauses give users control over sensitive information access during web-agent tasks.

name: InfraMind: A Novel Exploration-based GUI Agentic Framework for Mission-critical Industrial Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: InfraMind explores industrial management GUIs using virtual-machine snapshots and builds memory for planning and hierarchical state recognition. Its framework also studies knowledge distillation and safety checks on open-source and commercial data-center management platforms.

name: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on web interface reasoning, visual perturbation robustness, and safety-critical web understanding tasks.

name: Secure and Efficient Access Control for Computer-Use Agents via Context Space
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CSAgent, which combines static access policies with user intent and context and enforces them through an operating-system service. A supporting toolchain constructs and refines policies for agents using API, CLI and GUI interfaces.

name: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The reported contribution evaluates attack detection.
summary: Introduces WAInjectBench with a threat-model taxonomy and malicious and benign text-image datasets for web-agent prompt-injection detection. It compares detector families across explicit and less visible forms of injected content.

name: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.

name: Say One Thing, Do Another? Diagnosing Reasoning-Execution Gaps in VLM-Powered Mobile-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study measures reasoning and execution gaps across mobile interaction tasks.
summary: Introduces an evaluation framework for mobile GUI agents that compares actions implied by their reasoning with intended and executed actions to diagnose mismatches.

name: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Results are reported on WorkArena and WebArena; the injection result concerns a FocusAgent variant.
summary: Introduces FocusAgent, which uses a lightweight LLM to select task-relevant lines from web agents' accessibility-tree observations, reducing context size and exposure to prompt injection.

name: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Compliance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark addresses policy compliance in web-agent trajectories.
summary: Introduces PolicyGuardBench for detecting policy violations in full web-agent trajectories and their prefixes, and trains PolicyGuard as an efficient guardrail model.

name: Cross-Modal Content Optimization for Steering Web Agent Preferences
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The attacker can edit only their own listing's images and textual metadata.

name: Your Harness is Not Secure: Benchmarking Real-world Threat of Command Line Interface Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces AdvCLI, a sandbox benchmark for evaluating whether command-line agents carry out security-relevant operating-system tasks across multiple hosts.

name: Invisible to Humans, Triggered by Agents: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Mobile Vision-Language Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses the near-zero contact-touch signals of automated mobile agents to expose malicious visual content selectively during agent interactions. The paper combines this agent-only perceptual injection with HG-IDA* prompt optimization to study unauthorized cross-app actions.

name: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SecureWebArena with simulated interactive websites, an attack-vector taxonomy and labeled agent trajectories. Its evaluation separates failures in reasoning, behavioral traces and task outcomes across vision-language agent families.

name: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SusBench, an online benchmark that inserts dark-pattern designs into consumer websites for agent evaluation. A human study checks the realism of the interventions, and agent trials compare susceptibility across pattern types.

name: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HackWorld for evaluating visual computer-use agents in a capture-the-flag collection of web applications. The benchmark examines interface navigation and multistep planning during vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks.

name: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The short abstract supplies the framework and threat setting but no quantitative evaluation details.
summary: Proposes an in-browser fuzzing framework that uses language-model guidance to test indirect prompt-injection vulnerabilities in agentic browsers. The work focuses on unwanted actions triggered by webpage instructions under the browser agent's user privileges.

name: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. XML screen hierarchies appear in the abstract; Android deployment remains unspecified.
summary: Introduces CORE, which divides mobile UI hierarchies into semantic blocks and shares planning between local and cloud language models. Local ranking limits the screen information sent for cloud-side element selection, with a multi-round mechanism for correcting inadequate context.

name: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The experiments concern attacks across web tasks.
summary: Introduces Genesis, a red-teaming framework that generates adversarial injections for web agents and revises attack strategies using responses and interaction logs.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The attacks are evaluated within Android emulators.
summary: Introduces GhostEI-Bench, a benchmark that injects deceptive UI events into Android emulator workflows to assess mobile agents and analyze failures from actions and screenshots.

name: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces MobileRisk-Live and OS-Sentinel, combining a formal verifier for system-level violations with a multimodal judge for contextual risks in mobile GUI workflows.

name: Measuring the Security of Mobile LLM Agents under Adversarial Prompts from Untrusted Third-Party Channels
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Measures how untrusted third-party notifications, messages, and app content can hijack mobile LLM agents into executing unauthorized cross-app actions.

name: DualTAP: A Dual-Task Adversarial Protector for Mobile MLLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Applies dual-task adversarial perturbations to mobile screenshots to conceal personally identifiable information from untrusted MLLM routers while preserving agent task utility.

name: Can We Stop Malicious AI? KILLBENCH: A Benchmark for External AI Kill Switch Feasibility
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5).
summary: KillBench evaluates external prompt-style signals intended to halt maliciously operating web agents, across harmful scenarios and agent configurations.

name: Building Browser Agents: Architecture, Security, and Practical Solutions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Broader claims about the safety of general-purpose browsing are the paper's position.
summary: Reports architectural and security lessons from building a browser agent, including hybrid accessibility-tree and visual context, browser tooling and programmatic constraints. A WebGames evaluation accompanies the discussion of reliability and specialization.

name: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: BrowseSafe builds a benchmark of prompt injections in realistic HTML for browser agents and evaluates defenses against attacks that can affect agent actions.

name: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as planned.
summary: Presents a privacy evaluation framework for browser agents covering component weaknesses, website defenses, tracking, privacy-related prompts and personal-data leakage. The framework is applied to deployed browser-agent tools.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.

name: WebOperator: Action-Aware Tree Search for Autonomous Agents in Web Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on WebArena and WebVoyager.
summary: WebOperator uses tree search, action filtering, and path checks before replay to explore web tasks and backtrack while accounting for irreversible actions.

summary: Studies deceptive social-engineering web patterns targeting browser automation agents and proposes defenses against bait-based manipulation.

name: WebTrap Park: An Automated Platform for Systematic Security Evaluation of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces WebTrap Park, a platform that turns web-agent security risks into executable tasks and assesses concrete interactions with live pages. It compares agent frameworks without requiring modifications to their implementations.

name: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: NOVA separates trusted task planning from screen-derived observations by producing a branching plan before execution and resolving runtime values through perception. Its OSWorld study examines security and utility while identifying remaining risks from perception-driven branch steering.

name: Mind the Gap: Action Rebinding Attacks against Android GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies action-rebinding attacks in which an Android GUI agent’s planned input is redirected to a different application during the observation–action delay. The evaluation examines cross-application execution and the consequences of treating an earlier screen as the current action target.

name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.

name: MalURLBench: A Benchmark Evaluating Agents' Vulnerabilities When Processing Web URLs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: MalURLBench evaluates how LLM-based web agents handle disguised malicious URLs across attack scenarios; the paper also analyzes attack factors and proposes URLGuard.

name: GUIGuard-Bench: Toward a General Evaluation for Privacy-Preserving GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUIGuard-Bench, which annotates private regions in GUI trajectories with categories, risk levels, and relevance to the user’s task. It evaluates privacy recognition and the effect of screenshot protection on offline planning and task utility.

name: Okara: Detection and Attribution of TLS Man-in-the-Middle Vulnerabilities in Android Apps with Foundation Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Okara uses foundation-model-driven GUI agents to explore Android apps for TLS vulnerability detection, then applies instrumentation and classification to attribute vulnerable code.

name: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: SafePred uses world-model risk forecasts to guide action filtering and task replanning. Its desktop and web safety evaluations distinguish policy compliance, task success and success under the specified policy.

name: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebSentinel identifies suspicious webpage segments and checks each against its surrounding page context to detect and locate prompt injections. Its evaluation uses both contaminated and clean webpage datasets.

name: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: AutoElicit iteratively revises benign instructions using execution feedback to surface harmful unintended actions by computer-use agents in OS workflows.

name: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: MisActBench provides action-level labels for task alignment, while DeAction checks proposed computer-use actions and requests revisions through structured feedback. The paper separately evaluates offline detection and interactive operation in OSWorld and RedTeamCUA.

name: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs introduces generated interactive challenges intended to distinguish human users from GUI agents. The benchmark targets perception, memory, decisions and actions, with backend-supported challenge types designed for scalable instance generation.

name: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: MUZZLE evaluates web-agent exposure to indirect prompt injection by finding attack surfaces in agent trajectories and refining injected instructions from execution feedback.

name: Anonymization-Enhanced Privacy Protection for Mobile GUI Agents: Available but Invisible
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: An anonymization framework replaces sensitive screen content and instructions with consistent, type-preserving placeholders while mediating actions through a local interaction proxy. Experiments on AndroidLab and PrivScreen examine the privacy–utility trade-off when mobile GUI agents operate over these transformed interfaces.

name: Blind Gods and Broken Screens: Architecting a Secure, Intent-Centric Mobile Agent Operating System
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The reported comparison with a screen-based mobile assistant uses MobileSafetyBench.
summary: Analyzes security risks in screen-based mobile agents and proposes Aura, an agent runtime with structured interactions, app-agent isolation and mediated communication.

name: How Smart Is Your GUI Agent? A Framework for the Future of Software Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GAL is a conceptual framework.
summary: Proposes GUI Agent Autonomy Levels (GAL), a six-level framework for describing autonomy and benchmarking GUI agents that navigate web, desktop, and mobile software.

name: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent survey of the skill layer: CUA deployment and GUI grounding are explicit parts of the review, but its overall scope extends well beyond interface agents.
summary: This survey organizes agent skills by architecture, acquisition, deployment and security, including their role in computer-use systems and GUI grounding. It also proposes a permission and lifecycle governance framework for skill deployment.

name: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Formalizes and measures natural agentic oversharing when browser agents handle private user emails and calendars across live websites.

name: A Trajectory-Based Safety Audit of Clawdbot (OpenClaw)
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Audits Clawdbot safety through logged action and tool-call trajectories across local execution and web-mediated workflows, using automated and human review.

name: Atomicity for Agents: Exposing, Exploiting, and Mitigating TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Browser-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Identifies time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race vulnerabilities when web pages mutate between agent planning and action execution.

name: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies webpage injections that affect both screenshots and accessibility trees, then trains web agents through teacher imitation, supervised adversarial examples, and adversarial reinforcement learning. The evaluation tests defenses on MiniWoB++ and held-out tasks.

name: SlowBA: An efficiency backdoor attack towards VLM-based GUI agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces SlowBA, a backdoor attack on vision-language GUI agents that uses pop-up triggers to induce longer reasoning chains and increase response latency.

name: You Told Me to Do It: Measuring Instructional Text-induced Private Data Leakage in LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces ReadSecBench, a README-based benchmark for measuring whether high-privilege agents follow injected instructions that leak private data; a computer-use agent is evaluated.

name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.

name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.

name: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebPII provides synthetic e-commerce screenshots with fine-grained annotations for sensitive information, including partially filled forms and transaction identifiers. It also trains WebRedact to detect visual PII as a privacy component for computer-use agents.

name: ClawTrap: A MITM-Based Red-Teaming Framework for Real-World OpenClaw Security Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents a man-in-the-middle network red-teaming framework for evaluating autonomous OpenClaw agents under live traffic manipulation.

name: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: MANA combines visual, temporal and exploration signals to guide navigation toward mobile advertisements. It evaluates ad detection and interaction cost on commercial smartphones, including obfuscated-ad cases.

name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.

name: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes a split-compute browser defense pairing a local visual sentinel, a cloud planner, and deterministic policy enforcement against indirect prompt injection.

name: "What Did It Actually Do?": Understanding Risk Awareness and Traceability for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents an interview study of computer-use agent risks and AgentTrace, a prototype interface showing agent actions, resource access, permission history, and lasting changes.

name: Do Phone-Use Agents Respect Your Privacy?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MyPhoneBench to verify whether phone-use agents minimize personal data disclosure when filling forms during benign mobile tasks.

name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.

name: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces AgentHazard, a benchmark of harmful multi-step behavior by computer-use agents acting through tools, files, and execution environments.

name: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a safety evaluation of OpenClaw and the CIK taxonomy for analyzing how changes to a personal agent's persistent state affect attacks on its local and service access.

name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.

name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.

name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.

name: Preference Redirection via Attention Concentration: An Attack on Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Creating the attack requires white-box access to the model.
summary: Introduces PRAC, an adversarial-patch attack that redirects a computer-use agent's visual attention to steer product selection on an online shopping platform.

name: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The annotation describes risk calibration without asserting an unconditional safety guarantee.
summary: Introduces CORA, which calibrates a risk model to choose between executing and abstaining from mobile GUI actions, then diagnoses rejected actions to suggest interventions. Phone-Harm provides step-level safety labels for evaluating this safeguarding process.

name: The Blind Spot of Agent Safety: How Benign User Instructions Expose Critical Vulnerabilities in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported results concern human-crafted tasks across eight applications and two threat clusters.
summary: Introduces OS-BLIND, a computer-use agent safety benchmark for harmful outcomes arising from benign instructions and threats in task environments.

name: Mobile GUI Agent Privacy Personalization with Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported results use the authors' Privacy Preference Dataset.
summary: Proposes Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization (TIPO) to train mobile GUI agents for differing user privacy preferences across structurally different task trajectories.

name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.

name: Penny Wise, Pixel Foolish: Bypassing Price Constraints in Multimodal Agents via Visual Adversarial Perturbations
notes: Scope is screenshot-based interface understanding and safety. The retained abstract leaves the operating system and live transaction execution unspecified.
summary: Introduces PriceBlind, a visual perturbation method for controlled screenshot-based evaluation of price-constrained multimodal agents. The reported transfer experiments use a simplified single-turn coordinate-selection protocol.

name: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle
notes: Adjacent memory-security survey. Full-text Sections 3.1 and 3.3 discuss poisoned web observations persisted into later agent actions; the work covers a broader agent setting.
summary: Organizes security risks and defenses for persistent agent memory into six lifecycle phases and proposes five verifiable governance primitives.

name: Human-Guided Harm Recovery for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports human evaluation of recovery trajectories produced by the proposed scaffold.
summary: Introduces a preference-trained reward model for guiding computer-use agents out of harmful states and BackBench, a benchmark of recovery tasks.

name: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study examines UI changes between a desktop agent’s screenshot observation and action dispatch. Its pre-execution state checks address overlay and focus manipulation, while the reported DOM-injection blind spot limits the defense’s coverage.

name: OS-SPEAR: A Toolkit for the Safety, Performance,Efficiency, and Robustness Analysis of OS Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Provides an evaluation toolkit for joint safety, efficiency, and multimodal robustness analysis of operating-system GUI agents.

name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings.

name: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: AcademiClaw benchmarks OpenClaw agents on long academic workflows, scoring task completion in isolated Docker sandboxes with rubrics and a safety audit.

name: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Agentic Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates agentic browsers against classical web attacks and visual social-engineering lures beyond indirect prompt injection.

name: Constraining Host-Level Abuse in Self-Hosted Computer-Use Agents via TEE-Backed Isolation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: A TEE-backed design confines host operations by self-hosted computer-use agents, classifying and authorizing actions before constrained local execution.

name: Securing Computer-Use Agents: A Unified Architecture-Lifecycle Framework for Deployment-Grounded Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Survey of computer-use agent reliability and security across browsers, desktops, and mobile apps, using architecture and lifecycle views to map failures and controls.

name: WebTrap: Stealthy Mid-Task Hijacking of Browser Agents During Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on browser-agent tasks based on extended WASP and InjecAgent environments.
summary: WebTrap injects mid-task instructions into browser-agent navigation to steer an agent toward an attacker goal before it resumes the user's task.

name: OTora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework for Reasoning-Level Denial-of-Service in LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). WebShop is one of several agent settings used to evaluate the general attack framework.
summary: OTora generates attacks that increase reasoning and tool use in multi-step LLM agents while preserving task outcomes; evaluations include WebShop agents.

name: Don't Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DUDE combines asymmetric hybrid-reward learning with summaries of deceptive-interface failures to guide safer web actions. Its RUC benchmark evaluates deception susceptibility alongside ordinary task performance across interface scenarios.

name: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Directly analyzes browser-agent prompt-injection boundaries and WebArena task structure, advocating typed website operations.
summary: Argues for compiling web tasks into predefined execution graphs before exposing an agent to untrusted runtime content. name: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported identification results come from four web environments.
summary: A study shows that websites can infer the model behind a browser agent from passively recorded UI actions and timing traces across web tasks.

name: WARD: Adversarially Robust Defense of Web Agents Against Prompt Injections
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports results on out-of-distribution benchmarks and adaptive attacks.
summary: WARD guards web agents against prompt injections in HTML and visual interfaces, using web data and adaptive attacker–guard training.

name: PersonaFingerprint: Measuring Persona Inference on Modern Websites with LLM-Driven Browsing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The computer-use agent serves as browsing infrastructure for a privacy study.
summary: PersonaFingerprint studies persona inference from encrypted web traffic, using a persona-constrained computer-use agent to browse real websites and collect traces.

name: TClone: Low-Latency Forking of Live GUI Environments for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: TClone versions live GUI workspaces through snapshots, isolated forks, rollback and selective commit or merge. It separates fast branch creation from durable checkpoints using copy-on-write sharing, filesystem versioning and asynchronous checkpointing, with end-to-end agent-loop latency measurements.

name: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MIRAGE constructs mobile screenshot injections in ordinary user-content regions through localization, contextual payload generation and realism curation. Its evaluation separates visual realism from attack effectiveness against pixel-observing GUI agents.

name: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MaskClaw makes local Allow, Mask or Ask decisions before GUI screenshots leave a trusted environment, using visual evidence and personalized policy memory. Its benchmark and designed evolution scenarios test how corrections and edits can become privacy skills checked by a sandbox gate.

name: BraveGuard: From Open-World Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports guard evaluation on trajectory-level agent-safety benchmarks.
summary: Introduces BraveGuard, a framework that turns emerging threats and computer-use agent trajectories into training supervision for guards that monitor multi-step safety risks.

name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.

name: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CUA-HandCrafted, a browser-agent red-teaming benchmark that varies attack templates, tasks and system prompts. Its domain comparison and reproducibility audit caution against transferring browser-surface safety conclusions to coding agents or unreleased optimized injections.

name: MemVenom: Triggered Poisoning of Multimodal Memories in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports tests across multiple web-agent frameworks and vision-language models.
summary: Introduces MemVenom, a black-box attack that plants coordinated text and image content in web-agent memory to trigger retrieval and redirect later actions.

name: CAPED: Context-Aware Privacy Exposure Defense for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CAPED filters mobile screenshots before upload by combining task requirements, screen context and parsed UI elements to mask incidental private content. AndroidWorld and a controlled seeded privacy evaluation examine leakage reduction alongside task utility and prototype costs.

name: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: StakeBench evaluates prompt-injection harm to different stakeholders in shopping web-agent workflows. Its executable cases separate attack objectives and assess both outcomes and execution processes to reveal how the same attack pattern can affect different parties.

name: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluation injects seven deceptive patterns into existing web environments.
summary: Introduces WebDecept, a plugin for injecting deceptive e-commerce interface patterns during web-agent tasks and evaluating how multimodal agents respond.

name: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates action-level guardrails and full computer tasks with environment-dependent safety constraints, separating safe completion from nominal success.

name: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: FraudSMSWalker tests browser agents on bilingual SMS-to-webpage fraud judgments while hiding URL and reputation shortcuts. Its controlled chains include difficult benign login/payment cases and evaluate whether classifications remain supported by the visible message and page evidence.

name: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SkillHarness, a framework for computer-use agents to learn and reuse skills under safety constraints when interactions include prompt injections or pop-ups.

name: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MIRAGE evaluates targeted next-action hijacking from adversarial images restricted to legitimate third-party webpage regions. It combines diffusion-based image generation with execution-aware optimization and tests the constrained visual-injection setting on web-agent frameworks.

name: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Builds a logging framework that combines network/protocol fingerprints with browser interaction behavior to attribute web-agent traffic. A decision-tree classifier is evaluated across six agent implementations, human browsing and conventional crawlers.

name: Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Agent MechSuits, a framework that detects unsafe states and steers multi-turn CLI agents through hidden-representation interventions, alongside the MAS trajectory benchmark.

name: When AUC 0.998 Is Not Enough: A Candidate Evaluation Protocol for Hidden-State Probes of Indirect Prompt Injection in Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).

notes: Kotlin Android app for Android 11 (API 30) or later, published by KUAFUAI, with a floating-ball persona, voice input and output, an encrypted on-device notebook and scheduled scenes. One AccessibilityService is the entry point. ScreenController.kt renders the pruned accessibility tree as an outline with one line per element, an element id, a clickable mark and a centre in 0-1000 relative coordinates; for apps that draw their own pixels the model gets a screenshot (accessibility takeScreenshot, or MediaProjection per ScreenCapture.kt) overlaid with an 8-column by 12-row labelled grid, taps by cell and which third of it, and can request a zoomed view with a red crosshair before committing. A per-location guard refuses a fourth tap within 120 px of the same spot inside five minutes. Text goes in through the accessibility input channel on Android 13 or later, with ADBKeyboard as the fallback. LocalBrain.kt runs a non-streaming tool-calling loop against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint for a configurable number of steps (1 to 200); the brain can instead run elsewhere and reach the device over a WebSocket hub. The README states that the dispatcher stops before a purchase's final confirmation, never enters payment passwords, and types vault passwords without returning them to the model. name: Predicate Systems (formerly SentienceAPI)
notes: Predicate Systems Inc. was formerly SentienceAPI; www.sentienceapi.com redirects to this site. It has three parts. Predicate Authority is a Rust sidecar that evaluates local YAML policies and issues signed mandates before an action executes. Predicate Runtime, with Python and TypeScript SDKs, collects element geometry through a browser extension, gives the model a structured snapshot of element IDs, roles, text, importance scores and boxes (about 0.6-1.2k tokens per step by the publisher's estimate), executes the chosen action and runs assertions such as url_contains or exists; it runs standalone with Playwright or under browser-use, and an optional Gateway reranks elements with ONNX models. predicate-secure wraps frameworks such as browser-use, Playwright and LangChain with both checks. The documentation also covers Predicate Studio traces and Predicate Vault. New accounts start with 100 free credits.
summary: Runtime trust layer for browser agents: a sidecar checks each action against local policy before it runs, and SDKs turn pages into compact ranked element snapshots and verify outcomes with DOM assertions.

name: AdapAction: Adaptive Target Action Backdoor Attack against GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the CVF open-access landing page and PDF. A teacher model (for example Gemini 2.5 Pro) writes malicious reasoning trajectories drawn from a five-category malicious action library, and the agent learns them by supervised fine-tuning, which the paper calls Context-Aware Behavioral Imitation. Main results fine-tune Qwen2-VL-2B and Qwen2-VL-7B at a 0.1 poisoning ratio with a blended visual trigger; an AndroidWorld emulator deployment through Mobile-Agent-v3 is described in the supplementary material. The paper links no code release or arXiv version.
summary: Backdoor attack that fine-tunes GUI agents on teacher-written malicious trajectories, so a trigger makes the agent choose a harmful action fitting the current screen and instruction; tested on AitZ and AndroidControl.
